topline.headline: The R2 credential that unlocks the entire RUM saga has been READY the whole time — one fetch script ends three data-gated blockers at once.

items.summary: Build scripts/fetch-rum-from-r2.mjs — pull production RUM rows from the vaultspark-rum R2 bucket into data/rum-raw.ndjson via the READY cloudflare.r2 credential, then run rum:summary.
items.why: TASK_BOARD labels RUM-SAMPLE-UNLOCK '(Founder action: production RUM export access)' — but check-secrets shows cloudflare.r2 READY 4/4. This is a textbook CANON-019 phantom blocker: the Worker writes rum/raw/dt=<day>/<uuid>.json (security-headers-worker.js:305) and pull-rum-summary.mjs only ever reads LOCAL files — nobody ever built the R2→local hop. One script resolves the P1 blocker, and second-order it also feeds nav-sheet ux events toward MOBILE-SHEET-DEFAULT-SWAP readiness and seeds RUM-ANOMALY-CANARY. Three data-gated items share this single root cause.
items.recipe: Use S3-compat ListObjectsV2 + GetObject against the R2 endpoint with R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY via the secrets gateway (fallback: Cloudflare REST API with the cloudflare.studio cfut_ token). Write last-30-days objects to data/rum-raw.ndjson, run `npm run rum:summary`, report sample counts per route. Add `npm run rum:pull` script entry. No secrets in stdout (redact()).

items.summary: If the unlock yields ≥50 '/' samples: flip check-perf-budget --source=rum (+--strict if clean) and close the synthetic 13,060ms false alarm; else wire rum:pull into the session protocol so accrual is automatic.
items.why: check-perf-budget currently shows '/' desktop LCP 13060ms over budget — known to be a cold-TTFB synthetic-trace artifact (S161-S164 saga). Field truth replacing synthetic panic is the architectural end-state the S163 loop was built for; this item executes RUM-STRICT-FLIP the moment data exists instead of waiting passively. Log the flip in DECISIONS.md per the S164 carry instructions.
items.recipe: After item 1: read data/rum-summary.json; if samples('/')>=50 run check-perf-budget --source=rum, verify verdict, flip build:check to --source=rum (and --strict if green), log DECISIONS entry. If <50 samples, add rum:pull to closeout-autopilot pre-steps so every session accrues field data.

items.summary: When check-perf-budget flags a regression, auto-correlate the regression window against build-commit-map output and name the suspect commit range inside .cache/perf-fix-recipes.json.
items.why: S160's LCP regression cost a full manual bisect plan (revert nav-sheet, re-trace, suspect account-chip...). The repo already has both halves: perf-history.ndjson rows carry timestamps, and build-commit-map.mjs (S162) maps commits to shipped surfaces. Nobody joins them. A regression report that says 'between these 2 samples, these 4 commits touched assets in the ambient bundle' turns hours of bisecting into a glance — no other static-site repo does forensic perf attribution.
items.recipe: Extend check-perf-budget.mjs fix-recipe writer: for each over-budget group, find last-good and first-bad sample timestamps in data/perf-history.ndjson, run `git log --since --until --name-only` filtered to assets/+page HTML, cross-reference commit-map surface tags, emit suspectCommits[] in the recipe JSON. Self-test with a synthetic history fixture.

items.summary: Public-safe /api/site-health.json (p75 LCP/CLS from real visits + sample count, no IDs) + a 'measured from real visits' proof strip on /studio-pulse/.
items.why: S169 made professional studio posture a sitewide contract — release discipline with public proof. Once field RUM flows (item 1), the site can prove its own speed with visitor-measured numbers instead of self-reported lab traces. A studio that publishes its real-user p75 is making a craft statement competitors can't fake. Gated behind a sample threshold so it never renders on thin data.
items.recipe: Renderer script build-site-health.mjs reads data/rum-summary.json, emits api/site-health.json only when samples>=50 per route (publicSafe:true, no UAs/IDs). Small studio-pulse panel hydrates from it with an honest 'awaiting field samples' fallback state. Wire renderer into npm run build.

items.summary: Probe the Trusted Types soak counters in Workers KV via the broad cloudflare.studio cfut_ token — the named blocker is cloudflare.kv MISSING, but the studio token's scope includes KV.
items.why: TRUSTED-TYPES-ENFORCE-CANARY was evidence-deferred in S164 because the tt: KV soak was 'unreadable autonomously' (cloudflare.kv MISSING). But cloudflare.studio is READY and its declared scope is 'Workers/Pages/D1/R2/KV/DNS'. If the probe reads ~0 violations, the evidence half of the gate closes and only the founder device-verify remains — converting a credential blocker into a 5-minute founder step. CANON-019 demands this probe before the item stays human-blocked.
items.recipe: Script probe-tt-soak.mjs: REST list KV namespaces via cfut_ token (secrets gateway), find the tt:* keys the Worker writes, read counters, write docs/TT_SOAK_EVIDENCE_S172.md with violation counts + verdict. If token lacks KV scope after all, log the exact API error as durable evidence in the TASK_BOARD item.

items.summary: scripts/ark.mjs is MODULE_NOT_FOUND in this repo, yet AGENTS.md mandates Ark drain at /start and DRAIN-HUB-OBELISK-REPLIES waits on cargo that can never arrive. Restore the drain path.
items.why: This session's /start hit the gap live: the protocol ran `node scripts/ark.mjs drain --silent` into MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The S164 carry expects Hub and Obelisk replies — 5 blocked items cascade on the Obelisk answer — but this repo physically cannot receive cargo. An unread Obelisk reply could be sitting in the Ark transport right now while the TASK_BOARD calls it 'waiting'.
items.recipe: Vendor ark.mjs from ../vaultspark-studio-ops (or a thin shim that delegates to the sibling path with a reachability check + provenance header). Run drain immediately; surface any obelisk/hub cargo found. Add to check-protocol-scripts manifest so it can't silently vanish again.

items.summary: This session hit 7 MODULE_NOT_FOUNDs on protocol-referenced scripts (skill-profile, set-active-skill, credential-watch, ark, check-brief-staleness, sample-codebase, router). Teach check-protocol-scripts.mjs to classify and self-heal.
items.why: Every /start burns tokens on the same error stacks, and the S158 carry to 'resolve or explicitly allowlist unexpected absences' is still open four months later. A sentinel that classifies each missing reference (vendor-from-sibling / allowlist-with-known-fallback / stale-reference-to-remove) and auto-vendors when studio-ops is reachable turns recurring noise into a one-time fix — the S111 structural-gate pattern applied to the protocol surface itself.
items.recipe: Extend check-protocol-scripts.mjs with a REFERENCED_BY_SKILLS list + per-script policy map; emit .cache/protocol-script-heal-plan.json; implement --heal flag that copies vendorable scripts from the sibling with a `synced-from` header. Allowlist the genuinely studio-ops-only ones with documented fallbacks.

items.summary: Forensic decision dossier for the 3 feature-bearing orphan assets (membership-interview.js, vault-sdk.js, vaultsparked-proof.js): when wired, which commit orphaned them, rewire-vs-retire recommendation each.
items.why: The founder gate (SOUL #2: never half-bake membership) is legitimate, but the decision is currently impossible to make quickly — nobody knows HOW these became orphans. S135 proved the propagator class of bug 'replaces but never injects' script tags; if git history shows these were accidentally severed by a propagation pass rather than deliberately retired, the right call is rewire and it's nearly free. The dossier converts a stale P1 into a 30-second founder yes/no with evidence attached.
items.recipe: Per asset: `git log --follow --oneline -- assets/<file>` + `git log -S '<file>' --oneline -- '*.html'` to find the wiring-removal commit and its intent; inventory exported features; write docs/MEMBERSHIP_ORPHAN_DOSSIER_S172.md with a recommendation table (rewire target page / retire + archive) and effort per option.

items.summary: Generate docs/visual-proof/index.html — a side-by-side desktop/mobile gallery rendered from manifest.json — so LONGTAIL-VISUAL-PROOF-REVIEW is one click instead of six file-opens.
items.why: The S171 proof pack is sitting unreviewed partly because reviewing it means opening 6 PNGs individually. A static gallery page (local-only, not deployed) with route labels, capture dates, and non-blank scores makes the founder review take 30 seconds — and every future capture run regenerates it for free. Review friction is the silent killer of proof packs.
items.recipe: Script render-visual-proof-gallery.mjs reads docs/visual-proof/*/manifest.json, emits a dark-theme index.html with desktop|mobile pairs per route + metadata chips. Hook into capture-longtail-visual-proof.mjs tail. Keep it out of the deploy surface (docs/ is not served).

items.summary: Gated single-route production perf sample at closeout (disk OK + deploy parity OK) so the 43 'insufficient' perf-budget groups fill continuously instead of in audit bursts.
items.why: check-perf-budget reports 43 groups with insufficient samples — the history accrues only when someone remembers to run a trace. The S154 carry already designed this: one route per closeout, gated on disk headroom and parity. Continuous accrual also gives the commit-correlator (item 3) tighter regression windows to work with.
items.recipe: Add an optional closeout-autopilot step: rotate through routes (/, /membership/, /studio-pulse/), run measure-page-performance single-profile with --min-disk-mb=256 + parity check, append to perf-history.ndjson, skip silently when gates fail.

items.summary: Register testing surfaces in PROJECT_STATUS.json so the startup brief's WHERE TO TEST block stops rendering empty.
items.why: Every session's brief shows '(no testing surfaces registered)' — wasted prime real-estate in the first thing the founder reads. The surfaces already exist: live URL, staging, the ?nav=sheet flag page, /studio-pulse/. Registering them makes 'go verify on a real device' a copy-paste instead of a memory exercise.
items.recipe: Add testingSurfaces[] to PROJECT_STATUS.json ({label,url,note} entries for prod, staging, nav-sheet flag, studio-pulse); confirm render-startup-brief.mjs picks them up on next render.

items.summary: Refresh the two stale ops signals: IGNIS score (13d old, ⚠) and revenue signals (9d old, ⚠) via the studio-ops rescore path.
items.why: Both warnings have sat in SIGNALS for multiple sessions and each one is a single scripted command. Stale intelligence signals erode trust in the brief itself — when ⚠ is permanent, real warnings stop registering.
items.recipe: Run `node ../vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/ops.mjs rescore` for IGNIS; regenerate revenue signals via the studio-ops revenue script; confirm both flip to ✓ in a re-rendered brief.

Data-gated by design (S164 DECISIONS); item 1 feeds its telemetry rather than forcing the flip.
